response_kind: RFI response (capability statement, not a proposal)

card.situation:
NCI Oncology Clinical Trial System, Management and Support — a Sources Sought / RFI seeking small businesses capable of enterprise-level informatics, application development, modernization, and operational support for NCI's CTEP-ESYS clinical trial platform (HHS/NIH/NCI OLAO).
Reached the owner because Sooner Systems qualifies as a small business eligible to respond to this unrestricted sources-sought notice; a response is a capability statement only — no proposal or price is due.
reasons_for: Sooner Systems can satisfy the administrative submission requirements — electronic delivery in MS Word or PDF within the deadline — with 3.3 days remaining to close [req 53912490-descript-p0-a27ed7b0].

RMF/ATO documentation and FISMA/NIST vulnerability management experience (ACAS/Nessus) partially address the contract's security compliance requirements and could anchor a narrow cybersecurity section of a capability statement [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p8-e9536625].
The 24x7 NOC in Norman, OK and ITIL 4-certified Tier 1–3 help desk meet the after-hours logging and SLA response requirements for the user-support sub-task [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p11-af881e0d].
reasons_against: Sooner Systems has no biomedical or clinical trial informatics experience whatsoever — no CTEP-ESYS, protocol management, investigational agent management, or safety reporting capability — leaving Task Areas 3 and 4 entirely uncovered [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p3-ca2045b4].

The firm has no enterprise application development, maintenance, modernization, AI/ML integration, FHIR/CDISC interoperability, HHS EPLC, or Section 508 capability, accounting for 18 of 32 requirements rated as gaps [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p18-de9244fb; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p19-6f28203d; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p18-1b5bd551].

Past performance contract values ($0.74M–$2.1M) and scope (Army Corps help desk, FAA cybersecurity, OK National Guard M365 tenant migration) are far below the enterprise-scale clinical IT environment required, and neither record covers clinical or biomedical IT [profile: past performance, matched records — network administration/cybersecurity and IT help desk/desktop support only].

source_quotes: All capability statements sent in response to this Small Business Sources Sought notice must be sent electronically via email to Rosa Lopez, Contracting Officer at Rosa.Lopez@nih.gov in either MS Word or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) by September 17, 2026, 3:00PM ET.

matrix.firm_answer: Sooner Systems has no informatics, analytical engineering, or clinical research modernization capability. The firm provides IT help desk, network administration, and cybersecurity staffing only.

drafts.capability_statement:
Rosa Lopez, Contracting Officer
National Institutes of Health, NCI OLAO
Re: NCI Oncology Clinical Trial System, Management and Support — Sources Sought Notice 53912490fe424fd7a9e11fdaaf6a22a4

Sooner Systems LLC is a small business headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, responding to NCI's request for information on qualified sources for CTEP-ESYS support.

Sooner Systems provides IT infrastructure support, cybersecurity, and service desk services to federal civilian and defense agencies. Our relevant capabilities include:

**Cybersecurity & Compliance:** We hold hands-on experience with RMF/ATO documentation, vulnerability management using ACAS/Nessus, STIG implementation, and FISMA/NIST SP 800-37 RMF processes, demonstrated through our network administration and cybersecurity support engagement at the FAA Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center. We are CMMC Level 2 self-assessed.

**Cloud & Infrastructure Administration:** Our team has performed Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 administration, including a migration engagement for the Oklahoma National Guard.

**Service Desk & Operational Continuity:** We operate a 24x7 NOC in Norman, OK, staffed with ITIL 4- and Security+-certified personnel providing Tier 1–3 help desk support. We have delivered ticketing, SLA management, and after-hours incident logging for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

Sooner Systems acknowledges that CTEP-ESYS requires deep clinical trial informatics, application development, FHIR/CDISC interoperability, and AI/ML integration capabilities that currently exceed our core service lines. We are submitting this statement to register our interest and understand the government's requirements as this acquisition develops.

Point of Contact: [Name, Title, Phone, Email]
questions_for_co: Task Areas 3 and 4 (Operations, Maintenance, Enhancement, and Support; Information Management, Data Integration, and Interoperability) appear to require deep clinical trial application development and FHIR/CDISC interoperability expertise — does NCI anticipate that a prime contractor could satisfy these task areas through teaming arrangements with specialized subcontractors, or must the prime demonstrate all capabilities independently? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p3-fb3b3a7f; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p18-de9244fb]

The solicitation states that AI/ML capabilities must align with NIH's validated enterprise AI platform and that no independent commercial AI tools may be introduced without written COR approval — can NCI describe the current state of that enterprise AI platform and whether contractors are expected to bring AI/ML development staff, or primarily to govern and document existing platform integrations? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p13-c02ee21d; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p18-1b5bd551]

The RTO requirement specifies that critical CTEP-ESYS applications must be operational within 4 hours and fully operational within 24 hours of failure detection — does NCI expect the contractor to own application-level backup and recovery engineering, or will the government retain responsibility for application recovery while the contractor provides infrastructure and monitoring support? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p10-8086d5ac; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p9-da1ac9d7]

The zero-downtime migration requirement applies to IAM and all application modules during peak working hours — does NCI anticipate that the incumbent contractor will provide a structured knowledge transfer and that the migration plan will be co-developed with the government, or is the incoming contractor expected to independently assess and execute the full migration from NIH Building 12? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p26-71838b5c; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p8-f9e88dc6]

The HHS EPLC framework is required for all information systems development or enhancement tasks — will NCI provide EPLC templates, gate review schedules, and COR guidance to the contractor, or is the contractor expected to arrive with independent HHS EPLC implementation experience? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p11-631706fa]

Section 508 conformance is required across all ICT developed or maintained under this contract — does NCI currently have an accessibility testing environment, HHS Accessibility Checklist tooling, or a designated 508 coordinator who will work with the contractor, or must the contractor independently stand up all Section 508 testing and ACR reporting infrastructure? [req 53912490-b04ce8af-p19-6f28203d; req 53912490-b04ce8af-p20-55d108da]

reader.scope_summary: The government is buying enterprise-level technical and operational support services for CTEP-ESYS, NCI's integrated suite of applications that supports the conduct, oversight, and evaluation of NCI-sponsored oncology clinical trials, including protocol management, investigational agent management, safety reporting, and regulatory workflows. The work spans four task areas: task order management, infrastructure/hosting/security/continuity, operations/maintenance/enhancement/support, and information management/data integration/interoperability, while also requiring migration of all CTEP-ESYS applications from the NIH Building 12 data center to a Government-approved cloud or alternate data center no later than December 31, 2030. The contractor must also support modernization of legacy components, AI/ML integration via NIH's enterprise AI platform, Section 508 compliance, and FISMA/NIST/FedRAMP security controls, all without disrupting active clinical trial operations.
reader.incumbent_or_history: "The Contractor shall work with the predecessor Contractor to establish communication protocols and ensure that work operations are fully understood, and continuity of operations are maintained through the transition."
quotes: CTEP's Enterprise System (CTEP-ESYS) is NCI's enterprise system environment for supporting the conduct, oversight, and evaluation of NCI-sponsored oncology clinical trials.

The Contractor shall provide technical and operational support services for CTEP-ESYS applications, services, infrastructure, and information management capabilities in direct support of the conduct, oversight, and evaluation of NCI-sponsored oncology clinical trials.

It is anticipated that the NIH Building 12 data center will be decommissioned during the life of this contract, and all CTEP-ESYS applications and supporting components currently hosted in Building 12 shall be migrated to a Government -approved target environment no later than December 31, 2030, unless otherwise directed by the Government.

The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal regulations, HHS/NIH/NCI policies, and contract clauses governing information technology, security, privacy, accessibility, continuity, and records management, including but not limited to Section 508, FISMA, FedRAMP, HIPAA, HHS/NIH/NCI policy, and applicable NIST guidance.
Critical CTEP-ESYS applications must be operational within 4 hours and be fully operational within 24 hours of failure detection.

Any AI or ML capabilities proposed, developed, or implemented under this contract shall align with NIH's validated enterprise AI platform and shall not introduce independent commercial AI tools or contractor-managed AI infrastructure without explicit written approval from the COR.
Migration shall be performed with zero downtime for IAM and all application modules within CTEP-ESYS during peak working hours.

The Contractor shall work with the predecessor Contractor to establish communication protocols and ensure that work operations are fully understood, and continuity of operations are maintained through the transition.
All information systems development or enhancement tasks supported by the Contractor shall follow the HHS EPLC framework.

The goal of this acquisition is to identify qualified small business sources capable of providing enterprise-level informatics, application development, modernization, and operational support for CTEP-ESYS environment.
